1. A sensory mapping method for a human brain, the method comprising:
flattening the cortical surface of the human brain;
projecting functional imaging data onto the flattened surface;
smoothing the functional imaging data; and
generating a sensory map.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the smoothing comprises a topological smoothing method.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the smoothing comprises:
determining coordinates of each cortical area based on the functional imaging data;
repeating a process until the maximum absolute value of the Beltrami coefficient for each coordinate is less than one.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the smoothing comprises:
applying Beltrami coefficient to quantify diffeomorphism; and
modeling the smoothing in an optimization framework.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the flattening comprises a conformal parametrization method.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the flattening comprises:
applying harmonic mapping to a unit disk; and
refining repetitively parametric coordinate for each point on a parameter domain to produce conformal mapping.
7. The method of claim 1, further comprising rendering the sensory map with an image of stimuli that activate the cortical surface.
8. The method of claim 1, further comprising registering a plurality of sensory maps across different individuals.
9. The method of claim 8, further comprising analyzing the plurality of sensory maps in a common space.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein the registering is diffeomorphic.
11. A registration method that aligns a human brain sensory map of an individual to a predefined template, wherein the method comprises:
registering a plurality of sensory maps, each sensory map corresponding to a human brain of a different individual; and
analyzing the plurality of sensory maps in a common space.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the registering is diffeomorphic.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the registering comprises:
applying Beltrami coefficient to quantify diffeomorphism; and
modeling the registering in an optimization framework.
14. A sensory mapping method for a human brain, the method comprising:
flattening the cortical surface of the human brain;
projecting functional imaging data onto the flattened surface;
processing the functional imaging data to produce topological results; and
generating a sensory map.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein the processing comprises a topology-preserving cortical surface segmentation method.
16. The method of claim 14, wherein the processing comprises:
segmenting the cortical surface of the human brain by preserving the prior connectivity pattern of the cortical surface areas;
decoding the functional imaging data based on at least one topological condition within each cortical area; and
repeating the segmentation and decoding.
17. The method of claim 14, further comprising registering a plurality of sensory maps across different individuals.
18. The method of claim 17, wherein the registering is diffeomorphic
19. The method of claim 17, further comprising analyzing the plurality of sensory maps in a common space.
